questions.text: How high is your temperature, and how long have you had the fever?
questions.purpose: Characterise fever magnitude and duration to stratify severity
options: Not measured — feeling hot and unwell

questions.text: Are you experiencing rigors — severe uncontrollable shaking chills — alongside the fever?
questions.purpose: Rigors suggest bacteraemia or serious systemic infection requiring urgent assessment

questions.text: Have you recently travelled to a region where malaria, typhoid, dengue, or other tropical diseases are endemic?
questions.purpose: Recent travel to endemic regions requires fever-with-travel protocol

questions.text: Do you have a severe headache, stiff neck, aversion to bright light (photophobia), or a non-blanching rash?
questions.purpose: Meningism signs with non-blanching rash are red flags for bacterial meningitis/meningococcal disease

questions.text: Are you immunocompromised — from HIV, chemotherapy, steroids, or organ transplant?
questions.purpose: Fever in an immunocompromised patient is a medical emergency requiring immediate specialist assessment

questions.text: Have you identified a likely source of infection — cough, urinary symptoms, wound, diarrhoea?
questions.purpose: An identifiable infection source helps direct management pathway

questions.text: Has the fever persisted for more than 3 weeks despite initial antibiotic treatment or without an obvious cause?
questions.purpose: Fever of unknown origin (>3 weeks, >38.3°C, no diagnosis) requires specialist workup for occult infection, malignancy, or autoimmune disease
